req.title: Posts include author username
req.statement: The system shall join post rows with users so index/detail responses include the author's username.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that the index page (GET /) joins post rows with users so that each post's author username is present in the response. Tests must verify: (1) positive — known posts appear with their correct author usernames in the HTML response; (2) negative — a response without the JOIN would lack usernames, so we assert exact username strings are present; (3) boundary — the single-post edge case where exactly one author's username appears for that post, and the join column 'username' is not missing. We also cover multiple authors to catch mutations that might hard-code one username, and verify HTTP 200 exactly.

tests.name: test_index_includes_author_username_for_known_posts
preconditions: Database contains pre-loaded 20 posts with 5 users
actions: Create app with test config and temp database
GET / with test client
trace: R-FLASKR-024: index response includes author username via JOIN
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
data = r.data
assert b'Rahul' in data
assert b'James' in data
assert b'Anjali' in data
assert b'Ishaan' in data
assert b'Diya' not in data  # Diya (id=4) has no posts, should not appear
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_index_post_ordering_most_recent_first_with_username
preconditions: Post id=20 created='2025-04-01 10:30:37' by Rahul is the most recent post
Post id=18 created='2025-03-31 18:39:42' by Rahul is second most recent
actions: Create app with test config and temp database
GET / with test client
Check that the most recent post title appears before the second most recent in the HTML
expected: Title 'Heacon signal pulse' (post 20) appears before 'Eatrix cascade meridian' (post 18) in response
Both posts show 'Rahul' as author username
trace: R-FLASKR-024: JOIN result must be ordered DESC by created; boundary at most-recent post
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
data = r.data
pos_recent = data.find(b'Heacon signal pulse')

tests.name: test_index_username_field_present_after_new_post_created
preconditions: User Rahul (id=1) can log in with password 'stone'
actions: Create app with test config and temp database
Log in as Rahul
POST /create with a new post title and body
GET / and verify new post appears with 'Rahul' as author username
expected: New post title 'UniqueTestTitle2024XYZ' appears in response
Author username 'Rahul' appears in response alongside the new post
trace: R-FLASKR-024: newly created post must also include author username via JOIN
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert login_r.status_code == 302
create_r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'UniqueTestTitle2024XYZ', 'body': 'Test body content here.'})
assert create_r.status_code == 302
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
data = r.data
assert b'UniqueTestTitle2024XYZ' in data
assert b'Rahul' in data
os.unlink(path)
